key_insight: DuwatBench provides a focused multimodal benchmark for Arabic calligraphy—1,272 curated samples (~1,475 unique words) across six classical and modern styles—enabling systematic evaluation of models on stylized Arabic script that blends visual art and language.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of curated, style-aware datasets for Arabic calligraphy, which has limited multimodal models' ability to recognize, interpret, and preserve artistic forms of Arabic script.
method: Curate and standardize 1,272 high-quality calligraphic samples spanning six classical and modern Arabic styles with approximately 1,475 unique words.
Annotate each sample with word-level transcriptions, style labels and metadata, plus quality control to ensure consistency and cultural fidelity.
Define standardized evaluation tasks and protocols for multimodal models (e.g., stylized text recognition, style classification, image–text retrieval) to enable reproducible benchmarking.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a dedicated resource to train and evaluate OCR and multimodal models on artistic Arabic script, improving robustness for real-world, culturally-rich text and supporting preservation of visual heritage.
visual_elements: Dataset composition chart: bar/pie showing sample counts per calligraphic style and unique-word distribution.
Style mosaic: side-by-side image tiles of example samples from each of the six calligraphic styles with overlaid transcriptions.
Task flow diagram: input image ⇒ annotated data ⇒ benchmark tasks (recognition, style classification, retrieval) ⇒ evaluation metrics.
Performance mock-up/leaderboard: heatmap or table showing model performance across tasks and styles to highlight strengths/weaknesses.
paper_title: DuwatBench: Bridging Language and Visual Heritage through an Arabic Calligraphy Benchmark for Multimodal Understanding
paper_authors: Shubham Patle, Sara Ghaboura, Hania Tariq, Mohammad Usman Khan, Omkar Thawakar
